messages.author: 8bcb7cabc778c7da
messages.subject: defining modules in 3D
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to use the define.modules command to assign landmarks on a 3D skull, but I'm stuck on the code. I have a ply file and associated landmark list, but I'm not sure how to put them together to better see the anatomical locations of the landmarks while I am choosing. So far I managed to get the RGL window open with just the numbered landmarks, but I would like to also see the skull.

Is that possible, and if so, could someone please help me with code?

Thanks,
Christy

messages.author: 2c7106159c8e6d5b
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] defining modules in 3D
parts:
You can do it w just rgl and base functions....

# data
ply <- [read in your ply]
lms <- [p*3 matrix of landmarks]
lm.noms <- [landmark names in order of rows in lms]
lm.nums <- 1:nrow(lms)

# Plotting ply and landmarks.
# specular is one way to control glare
# alpha level sets transparency
plot3d(ply, col = adjustcolor("lightgrey", .3), alpha = .3, specular = 1, 
                    axes = F, box = F, xlab = "", ylab = "", zlab = "", main = "")
spheres3d(lms, radius = .1, color = "red")

# Plotting landmark names and/or ordered landmark numbers
# you may want to choose one or the other below
text3d(lms, texts = lm.noms, adj=1)
text3d(lms, texts = lm.nums, adj=c(0,1))

parts:
Following up...

Christy emailed her files to me directly. We're not sure what happened on her first try, but the code works. I've attached the R script, and I've pasted the images below, followed by a couple of instructions for the script.
 
Script instructions: Put the script in the same folder as the nts and ply files. The script assumes you use Rstudio. You will have to install and load into the session a package called rstudioapi. It has a function (see line 6 of script) which gives you the path to the script you are currently using. Once you know the location of your script, it's easy to navigate to and open other files in the same folder, or in nearby folders. If you don't use Rstudio, you'll skip lines 5-8, and modify lines 11 and 12 to read in your files.

David
